title: Death and the Intermediate State
definition: Death is the separation of soul and body; the intermediate state is conscious existence after death before the final resurrection and judgment.
summary: After death, believers enter Christ's presence while unbelievers enter conscious judgment, both awaiting future resurrection and final judgment.
christFocus: Jesus conquered death and promises eternal life to those who trust Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Death entered the world through sin and remains an enemy. Scripture teaches that death is not the end of existence. After death, believers enter the presence of Christ while unbelievers enter a state of conscious judgment, both awaiting the future resurrection and final judgment.

This truth avoids vague ideas about death and rejects the idea that all people simply disappear or enter the same condition. Scripture speaks with both comfort and warning.

For believers, death is sorrowful but not hopeless. To depart and be with Christ is far better. Yet final hope still awaits the resurrection of the body and the new creation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People are often confused, afraid, or vague about what happens after death. This doctrine matters because it gives comfort to believers, seriousness to unbelievers, and clarity about the hope of resurrection.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Prepare for death by trusting Christ now. Comfort grieving believers with the hope of being with the Lord, and let the reality of judgment give urgency to Gospel witness.
